source.title: What is the functional role of SAE errors?

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or cutoff; the text is a full post and includes comments.
record.tranche_reason: The post tests whether SAE features account for model behavior by ablating SAE error terms and restoring selected SAE features. Its results refine the claim that SAE features are complete units, but it does not test the original toy-network superposition experiment.
record.gate_note: The post reports ablation, restoration, and probing outcomes on Gemma-2 2B and its SAE representations. Crosscoder training is described as unsuccessful and supplies no test of the hypothesis. Results cited from other work are not recorded as findings here. Several plot outcomes are described qualitatively without exact values.
record.test_reason: In Gemma-2 2B with Gemma Scope SAEs, the post ablates SAE error nodes and restores SAE features on the SVA-RC task. This directly measures whether SAE features alone carry the model's task computation, which is the completeness part of V5. It does not study toy models, neuron polysemanticity or feature dimensionality. The rows measure circuit faithfulness rather than neuron spread or feature recovery, so they do not bear on V4.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say their ablation results somewhat lower the probability of an alternative 'path through the error nodes'. They add that late error ablation barely matters while late feature ablation does. On probing, they conclude the AdamW advantage of SAE-error probes is likely an artifact: with logistic regression, the residual stream is best.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE-based sparse feature circuits, faithfulness evaluation, residual-error ablations, feature restoration, and probing in Gemma-2 2B; does not reproduce the original toy-network feature-sparsity and dimensionality experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome changes with mean versus zero ablation, which error-node layers are ablated, which SAE feature layers and how many features are restored, whether the earlier 'that' token and MLP/attention nodes are included, and probe optimizer (AdamW versus logistic regression).

fits_no_version.finding: SAE error nodes in early-mid layers appear to carry intermediate steps needed to compute late-mid SAE features. The authors frame this as possible cross-layer superposition, and an attempted crosscoder test failed to train.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Features can be superposed across layers, leaving their intermediate representations in per-layer SAE errors.

record.problems: The authors describe the results as preliminary and partial. The circuit experiments focus on one model and task; ablation results may be affected by self-repair and out-of-distribution effects. Feature selection is a rough top-K AtP heuristic, and the authors say their feature baselines may be flawed. Crosscoder analysis did not produce a successful trained model. Many plotted outcomes have no exact numerical values in the text, and the post does not report statistical tests for the key restoration comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No result-bearing findings were omitted. The attempted crosscoder training difficulties and proposals for future work were not extracted as rows because they do not report a test outcome bearing on the claim.

untested.parts: No toy models, no sparsity sweep, no geometry.
No neuron polysemanticity or capacity-allocation analysis.
Does not measure how features spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover ground-truth features.
Stability, canonicity and comparison across dictionaries are untested. Only completeness on one task in one model is tested.
Not tested; multidimensional features are raised only in a comment.

missing.what: Replicating Marks et al., ablating residual error nodes is much more destructive to circuit faithfulness than ablating MLP and attention error nodes.
After filtering out low-confidence prompts, faithfulness of a ~1K-node SAE circuit falls from 0.833 to 0.526, with a bimodal distribution (works about half the time).

record.verdict_notes: V4 links were removed from all rows: these are faithfulness measures of SAE circuit completeness, not measures of feature spread across neurons or of SAE feature recovery. The probing rows are unreliable by the authors' own account. This is a preliminary, non-peer-reviewed post on a single model and task.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, feature-count-to-dimension sweep, or test of sparsity-dependent geometry.
No test of polysemantic neurons, feature competition for dimensions, or importance-dependent allocation.
No test of causes of polysemantic neurons independent of capacity pressure.
The post tests SAE feature interventions in Gemma-2 2B, but does not measure how many neurons encode each feature or compare SAE features with a ground-truth feature set.

Tests functional completeness for selected tasks and settings, not stability across models, datasets, training stages, or alternative dictionaries; does not establish whether SAE features are canonical units generally.
No test of whether features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional subspaces.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2 2B, SVA-RC, residual SAE error nodes ablated without restoration
relationships.reason: With residual errors ablated, SAE features keep faithfulness at 0.13 (R1). Ablating errors in layers 11–18 gives 0.3 (R15). Error ablation in layers 14–17 is the most damaging window (R10), and in size-8 windows it is more destructive than ablating the top-10 features (R14).
relationships.display_finding: SAE features alone kept a faithfulness of 0.13, or 0.3 when errors were ablated only in layers 11–18. Error ablation did the most damage in layers 14–17, and in 8-layer windows it was more destructive than ablating the top-10 features.

source_check.reason: R1 and R15 retain faithfulness of 0.13 and 0.3; R10 and R14 show damaging but unquantified window effects. These demonstrate incomplete SAE sufficiency, which the supplied rules classify as partial and limits_scope, rather than an absent or reversed effect.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2 2B, SVA-RC, errors ablated but selected late-mid SAE features restored, or only late errors ablated
relationships.reason: Restoring about 10–25 features from layers 18–21 recovers faithfulness to 0.6–1.0, depending on layers, number of features and mean versus zero ablation (R3–R7, R9). Late error ablation has little effect (R11). Restoring the top-1 feature does nothing (R2). The SAE's shortfall is therefore concentrated in the inputs to a few late-mid features.
relationships.display_finding: With SAE errors ablated, restoring about 10–25 features from layers 18–21 brought faithfulness back to 0.6–1.0 depending on layers, feature number and mean versus zero ablation, while late error ablation had little effect and restoring the top-1 feature did nothing.
